this is a bookkeeping instrument holding the amount or value of something by registering the movements in plus and min when events happen which have an impact on the position .
The term "account" is usually associated to an accounting or bookkeeping concept to hold the financial or stock state of a business concept. An account will typically group the debit and credit entries for a specific aspect of the business resulting from transactions,
Often accounts are represented as a T-account which is a visual aid used to depict an account. Above the top portion of the T would be the account title. On the left-side of the base of the T would be any debit amounts; on the right-side would be the credit amounts.
A commonly used bookkeeping method is the double-entry method. This means that every transaction has at least 2 movements. If a customer pays 100 € in cash , there is
a decrease in the amount that the customer owes to the company (the customer position is decreased)
an increase in the amount that the company has in cash (the cash position is increased)
An account can be assign to one or more ledgers. A ledger is a group of accounts for a certain purpose. If there is need for multiple ledgers because of multiple purpose, an account can perfectly wel assigned to multiple ledgers. When Ledgers are in real physical books, this is not possible. When ledgers are digital, accounts can be grouped into multiple groups at the same time. This practice is very rarely taught into courses for accounting, but in digital accounting, it is common practice.
Examples:
stock account of a shop, cash register, bank account, financial accounting account, customer account, supplier account, ...
Bank Account BE12 1234 5678 9012 : is an individual banking account
Accounts Payable , is a collective account keeping the balance of the amounts to pay by the organisation to its suppliers. The balance is the result of the financial movements related to suppliers . This account is managed usually in a General Ledger
Supplier Account X, is an individual account keeping the balance of the amounts to pay by the organisation to an individual supplier. The balance is the result of the financial movements related to an individual supplier. This account is managed usually in a sub-ledger.
Stock Account x , is an individual account keeping the balance of the amounts in stock of a specific good.

Supplier Account X, is an individual account keeping the balance of the amounts to pay by the organisation to an individual supplier. The balance is the result of the financial movements related to an individual supplier. This account is managed usually in a sub-ledger.
Stock Account x , is an individual account keeping the balance of the amounts in stock of a specific good.

A list of values which specifies the category of agreement. Agreement type is very often referred to "product". But, the term "product" does not cover all kinds of agreements. Other one can classify agreement based on "duration" like short-term agreement or long-term agreement.

Asset.documentation:
An object classified as something of value.
It is s ome tangible or intangible thing that the bank has ownership and/or influence over and has one or more inherent uses or purposes that create commercial value
Comment
BIAN has defined the likely assets found in any bank and uses this approach to isolate the specific types of asset that are acted on by the ServiceDomains. The role or purpose of each and every ServiceDomain is to apply its specific functional pattern to instances of one type of asset.
Is the tangible or intangible item that can have associated 'replacement' value/worth and purpose/use for which the bank has ownership or some level of control. It is exploited/leveraged in the execution of business through the application of some business behavior/control as effected by a ServiceDomain. Some asset types are obvious - for example a machine or building, some are intangible but easily identified such as knowhow, knowledge, relationships, reputation. Some are less obvious - most common is the 'capacity to perform' type which applies to many BIAN Service Domains. For example in the case of product fulfillment and support activities like party authentication the asset is the bank's possession of the capacity to perform these activities - the combination of the people/processes/systems to execute if you will...

Asset Securitization Arrangement.documentation:
An arrangement which involves putting together a claim on particular assets which is then sold as a negotiable security in the financial markets.
What is Securitization?
Securitization is the procedure where an issuer designs a marketable financial instrument by merging or pooling various financial assets into one group. The issuer then sells this group of repackaged assets to investors.
Securitization is the process of taking an illiquid asset or group of assets and, through financial engineering, transforming it (or them) into a security.
Securitization, the practice of pooling together various types of debt instruments (assets) such as mortgages and other consumer loans and selling them as bonds to investors.
securitization is an arrangement which involves putting together a claim on particular assets of a business which is then sold as a negotiable security in the financial markets.
Pooling securities into an ABS is a process called securitization.
Asset-backed securities (ABS) are financial securities backed by assets such as credit card receivables, home equity loans, and auto loans.

Bank Guarantee Agreement.documentation:
An agreement made by a bank or other financial instituation, where the bank assures or guarantees a beneficiary to pay a debt in case the actual customer who owes the money cannot pay.
Bank Guarantee vs Letter of Credit
- A bank guarantee is a promise from a lending institution that ensures the bank will step up if a debtor can't cover a debt.
- Letters of credit are also financial promises on behalf of one party in a transaction and are especially significant in international trade.
Letter of credit is an financial document for assured payments, i.e. an undertaking of the buyer's bank to make payment to seller, against the documents stated. A bank guarantee is a guarantee given by the bank to the beneficiary on behalf of the applicant, to effect payment, if the applicant defaults in payment.

DateTime.documentation:
A date time identifies a date and time of day to various common resolutions: year, month, week, day, hour, minute, second, and fraction of second. (UN/CEFACT)
A particular point in the progression of time defined by a mandatory date and a mandatory time component, expressed in either UTC time format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ), local time with UTC offset format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sss+/-hh:mm), or local time format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sss). These representations are defined in "XML Schema Part 2: Datatypes Second Edition - W3C Recommendation 28 October 2004" which is aligned with ISO 8601. (ISO20022)

1) beginning / end of calendar day
00:00:00 = the beginning of a calendar day
24:00:00 = the end of a calendar day
2) fractions of second in time format
Decimal fractions of seconds may be included. In this case, the involved parties shall agree on the maximum number of digits that are allowed.

The Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA) is a law that requires foreign financial institutions to report on the assets held by U.S. account holders. FeatureTypeValues.documentation:
Features in banking and business can be classified into different categories based on their purpose, functionality, and the value they provide. Here's a structured way to classify them:
1. Based on Functionality
Core Features: Essential functionalities required for the basic operation of a product or service.
Examples: Account creation, deposits, withdrawals, balance inquiries in banking.
Value-Added Features: Additional services that enhance customer experience and satisfaction.
Examples: Cashback rewards, financial planning tools, or loyalty programs.
2. Based on Service Type
Customer-Facing Features: Visible to customers and directly used by them.
Examples: Mobile banking apps, self-service kiosks, and chatbots.
Back-End Features: Operational features that support business processes but are not directly visible to customers.
Examples: Fraud detection systems, transaction monitoring, and risk assessment tools.
3. Based on Delivery Channel
Digital Features: Offered through online platforms or apps.
Examples: Biometric login, real-time notifications, and online fund transfers.
Physical Features: Provided at physical locations or through tangible means.
Examples: ATM cash withdrawal, in-branch consultations.
4. Based on the Target Audience
Retail Features: Designed for individual customers or small businesses.
Examples: Personal loans, savings accounts, and credit cards.
Corporate Features: Tailored for businesses or large organizations.
Examples: Cash management solutions, trade financing, and payroll processing.
5. Based on Purpose
Transactional Features: Facilitate day-to-day transactions.
Examples: Payments, transfers, or POS (Point of Sale) services.
Analytical Features: Provide insights, reports, or tracking capabilities.
Examples: Expense categorization, investment performance analysis.
Support Features: Assist customers in resolving issues or queries.
Examples: 24/7 customer support, AI-powered chatbots.
6. Based on Innovation Level
Standard Features: Common across most competitors in the industry.
Examples: Basic savings accounts, ATM access.
Differentiating Features: Unique or advanced features that set a company apart.
Examples: Cryptocurrency wallets, eco-friendly investment options.
7. Based on Technology
AI-Driven Features: Leverage artificial intelligence for smarter operations.
Examples: Fraud detection, personalized financial advice.
Cloud-Based Features: Hosted on cloud platforms for better scalability and availability.
Examples: Online document storage, remote account management.
8. Based on Compliance

Examples: KYC (Know Your Customer) verification, AML (Anti-Money Laundering) checks.

Examples: Encryption, two-factor authentication.

documentation_sections.documentation:
Features in banking and business can be classified into different categories based on their purpose, functionality, and the value they provide. Here's a structured way to classify them:
1. Based on Functionality
Core Features: Essential functionalities required for the basic operation of a product or service.
Examples: Account creation, deposits, withdrawals, balance inquiries in banking.
Value-Added Features: Additional services that enhance customer experience and satisfaction.
Examples: Cashback rewards, financial planning tools, or loyalty programs.
2. Based on Service Type
Customer-Facing Features: Visible to customers and directly used by them.
Examples: Mobile banking apps, self-service kiosks, and chatbots.
Back-End Features: Operational features that support business processes but are not directly visible to customers.
Examples: Fraud detection systems, transaction monitoring, and risk assessment tools.
3. Based on Delivery Channel
Digital Features: Offered through online platforms or apps.
Examples: Biometric login, real-time notifications, and online fund transfers.
Physical Features: Provided at physical locations or through tangible means.
Examples: ATM cash withdrawal, in-branch consultations.
4. Based on the Target Audience
Retail Features: Designed for individual customers or small businesses.
Examples: Personal loans, savings accounts, and credit cards.
Corporate Features: Tailored for businesses or large organizations.
Examples: Cash management solutions, trade financing, and payroll processing.
5. Based on Purpose
Transactional Features: Facilitate day-to-day transactions.
Examples: Payments, transfers, or POS (Point of Sale) services.
Analytical Features: Provide insights, reports, or tracking capabilities.
Examples: Expense categorization, investment performance analysis.
Support Features: Assist customers in resolving issues or queries.
Examples: 24/7 customer support, AI-powered chatbots.
6. Based on Innovation Level
Standard Features: Common across most competitors in the industry.
Examples: Basic savings accounts, ATM access.
Differentiating Features: Unique or advanced features that set a company apart.
Examples: Cryptocurrency wallets, eco-friendly investment options.
7. Based on Technology
AI-Driven Features: Leverage artificial intelligence for smarter operations.
Examples: Fraud detection, personalized financial advice.
Cloud-Based Features: Hosted on cloud platforms for better scalability and availability.
Examples: Online document storage, remote account management.
8. Based on Compliance
Regulatory Features: Designed to comply with laws and regulations.
Examples: KYC (Know Your Customer) verification, AML (Anti-Money Laundering) checks.
Security Features: Protect customer data and transactions.
Examples: Encryption, two-factor authentication.

Financial Instrument Position.documentation:
The position of a financial instrument
What is a Position?
A position is the amount of a security, commodity or currency which is owned by an individual, dealer, institution, or other fiscal entity. They come in two types: short positions, which are borrowed and then sold, and long positions, which are owned and then sold. Depending on market trends, movements and fluctuations, a position can be profitable or unprofitable. Restating the value of a position to reflect its actual current value on the open market is referred to in the industry as "mark-to-market." (Investopedia)
https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/position.asp#:~:text=A%20position%20is%20the%20amount,are%20owned%20and%20then%20sold .

Financial Liability.documentation:
Financial liability: any liability that is:
- A contractual obligation: to deliver cash or another financial asset to another entity; or to exchange financial assets or financial liabilities with another entity under conditions that are potentially unfavourable to the entity; or
- A contract that will or may be settled in the entity's own equity instruments and is
--a non-derivative for which the entity is or may be obliged to deliver a variable number of the entity's own equity instruments or
--a derivative that will or may be settled other than by the exchange of a fixed amount of cash or another financial asset for a fixed number of the entity's own equity instruments. For this purpose the entity's own equity instruments do not include: instruments that are themselves contracts for the future receipt or delivery of the entity's own equity instruments; puttable instruments classified as equity or certain liabilities arising on liquidation classified by IAS 32 as equity instruments
https://www.iasplus.com/en/standards/ias/ias32
https://www.accountingtools.com/articles/2017/5/10/financial-liability

Investment Portfolio.documentation:
A set of financial assets owned by an investor
Comment:

- Investors aim for a return by mixing these securities in a way that reflects their risk tolerance and financial goals. https://smartasset.com/investing/what-is-an-investment-portfolio
- Portfolio investments are passive investments, as they do not entail active management or control of the issuing company.
- A portfolio investment is an asset that is purchased in the expectation that it will earn a return or grow in value, or both.
- A portfolio investment is passive, unlike a direct investment, which implies hands-on management.
- Risk tolerance and time horizon are key factors in selecting any portfolio investment.

Journal.documentation:
A log of financial transactions in chronological order and kept in the accounting system in the format of bookkeeping.
Some refer to the journal as the book of original entry, since the entries are first recorded in a journal. From the journal the entries will be posted to the designated accounts in the general ledger. With manual systems there are likely to be a sales journal, purchases journal, cash receipts journal, cash disbursements journal, and the general journal. With computerized accounting systems, it is likely that the general journal will be used sparingly. The software is likely to record the other transactions automatically as invoices are entered, checks are prepared, receipts processed, etc.. (see accounting coach).

Lease Agreement.documentation:
Definition:
A (Debt) agreement between the lessor (owner of the asset) and the lessee (user of the asset) whereby the lessor purchases an asset for the lessee and allows him to use it in exchange for periodical payments called lease rentals or minimum lease payments (MLP).
Comments:
At the conclusion of the lease period, the asset goes back to the lessor (the owner) in an absence of any other provision in the contract regarding compulsory buying of the asset by the lessee (the user). There are four different things possible post-termination of the lease agreement.
All the future actions of lessee and lessor relevant to the asset under the lease are guided by this lease agreement.
The lease agreement is a written legal document signed by both the lessor and the lessee and thereby agreeing to the terms and conditions mentioned in the agreement of lease.
Not only does the agreement cover the basic details like the asset, lease rental etc but it extensively covers all the important points which may form part of a conflict between the parties during the period of lease.
A good lease agreement will have crystal clarity on all the terms just like the constitution of a country.

Market Segment.documentation:
An identifiable group of individuals, families, businesses, or organizations, sharing one or more characteristics or needs in an otherwise homogeneous market. Market segments generally respond in a predictable manner to a marketing or promotion offer (Business Dictionary) .... Read more: http://www.businessdictionary.com/definition/market-segment.html
A market segment is a group of people in a homogeneous market who share common marketable characteristics (Investopedia). https://www.investopedia.com/terms/m/market-segment.asp
The criteria for a market segment are that there is homogeneity among the segment's main needs, the segment must be unique, and the segment's members must produce a common reaction to marketing tactics.
Common market segment traits include interests, lifestyle, age, and gender.

PaymentAmountAndCurrency.documentation:
In payment systems (especially ISO 20022 / SWIFT), there are different "types of amounts" defined at the debtor (payer) and creditor (payee) level, because the amount can change as it moves through banks, fees, and FX conversion.
At the Debtor (Payer) Level:
a) Instructed Amount: The amount the debtor asks their bank to transfer (e.g., "Send 100 EUR").
b) Equivalent Amount: If the debtor's account is in a different currency, this is the converted equivalent (e.g., 100 USD = 91 EUR).
c) Debtor Account Amount: The actual amount debited from the debtor's account (after currency conversion, possibly including charges).
At the Creditor (Payee) Level:
d) Interbank Settlement Amount: The amount exchanged/settled between the banks (may be in a different settlement currency, e.g., USD).
e) Creditor Account Amount: The amount credited to the creditor's account in their account currency (e.g., GBP).
f) Net / Received Amount: The final amount the creditor actually receives after any deductions (e.g., fees).

Subledger.documentation:
Definition of Subsidiary Ledger
A "book" containing Subledger Accounts.
A subsidiary ledger is a Ledger that contains the details to support a general ledger account.
For instance, the subsidiary ledger for accounts receivable contains the information for each of the company's credit sales to customers, each customer's remittance, return of merchandise, discounts, and so on. With these details in the subsidiary ledger, the Accounts Receivable account in the general ledger can report summary amounts for the accounts receivable activity.
Examples of Subsidiary Ledgers
By having the details of the accounts receivable activity in a subsidiary ledger, employees in a company's credit department of a company can access the credit sales information without having access to any information in the general ledger.
In job order costing systems, the job cost sheets (or job cost records) will serve as the subsidiary ledger containing the details for the general ledger account Work in Process. The Work in Process account will now be a control account containing summary amounts for direct materials, direct labor, factory overhead applied, transfers to finished goods, etc. Manufacturing personnel will have full access to the job cost sheets without having access to other information in the general ledger.
Since companies are integrating accounting records with their other information into one database, I assume there will be less use of the term subsidiary ledgers in the future. There will likely be reports generated to provide the information formerly contained in the subsidiary ledger.

Asset Type.documentation:
Some tangible or intangible thing that the bank has ownership and/or influence over and has one or more inherent uses or purposes that create commercial value. (BIAN)
Comment
BIAN has defined the likely assets found in any bank and uses this approach to isolate the specific types of asset that are acted on by the ServiceDomains. The role or purpose of each and every ServiceDomain is to apply its specific functional pattern to instances of one type of asset.
Is the tangible or intangible item that can have associated 'replacement' value/worth and purpose/use for which the bank has ownership or some level of control. It is exploited/leveraged in the execution of business through the application of some business behavior/control as effected by a ServiceDomain. Some asset types are obvious - for example a machine or building, some are intangible but easily identified such as knowhow, knowledge, relationships, reputation. Some are less obvious - most common is the 'capacity to perform' type which applies to many BIAN Service Domains. For example in the case of product fulfillment and support activities like party authentication the asset is the bank's possession of the capacity to perform these activities - the combination of the people/processes/systems to execute if you will...

Booking Scheme.documentation:
A booking schema (also called posting schema, accounting schema, or journal entry template) is a set of predefined accounting rules that tell a system which accounts to debit and credit when a specific business event occurs.
A Booking Schema is a predefined set of rules or templates that determine how financial transactions from business events are posted to accounts in the ledger.
It maps business events (like loans, payments, fees, or sales) to the correct ledger accounts and often specifies:
- Debit and credit accounts
- Posting rules (amounts, dimensions, currencies)
- Transaction types and subledger sources
In essence, a booking schema translates business events into accounting entries.

Card Payment Authorization.documentation:
Authorisation of a card payment instruction or transaction.
Once the card and the cardholder have been successfully authenticated,
authorisation is usually requested. However, this stage may be skipped in
some cases (e.g. for transactions below a certain value), at the risk of the card acceptor. The terminal forwards the request for authorisation to the acquirer, to the acquirer's processor or to the card scheme. If the acquirer and the issuer are one and the same, such transactions are referred to as "on-us" transactions and the acquiring bank carries out the authorisation itself. For transactions other than "on-us" transactions (i.e. where the issuer and the acquirer are not the same), authorisation may be obtained offline or online. In offline authorisations, the request is handled directly by the card acceptor's terminal. In most cases, however, the authorisation is online and the request passes from the terminal to
the acquirer. The acquirer may directly authorise or refuse the transaction, but will in most cases pass the transaction to a switching centre. The switching centre transfers the authorisation request and transaction information to the appropriate issuer or the authorisation platform (which may be the card scheme or a third-party service provider). The authorisation process usually includes checking the card details against a list of cards that have been reported as having been lost,
stolen, used fraudulently or counterfeited. Checks on balances and card limits (i.e. daily and monthly limits) are usually also carried out. (Payment System ECB)

The terminal forwards the request for authorisation to the acquirer, to the acquirer's processor or to the card scheme. If the acquirer and the issuer are one and the same, such transactions are referred to as "on-us" transactions and the acquiring bank carries out the authorisation itself. For transactions other than "on-us" transactions (i.e. where the issuer and the acquirer are not the same), authorisation may be obtained offline or online. In offline authorisations, the request is handled directly by the card acceptor's terminal. In most cases, however, the authorisation is online and the request passes from the terminal to
the acquirer. The acquirer may directly authorise or refuse the transaction, but will in most cases pass the transaction to a switching centre. The switching centre transfers the authorisation request and transaction information to the appropriate issuer or the authorisation platform (which may be the card scheme or a third-party service provider). The authorisation process usually includes checking the card details against a list of cards that have been reported as having been lost,
stolen, used fraudulently or counterfeited. Checks on balances and card limits (i.e. daily and monthly limits) are usually also carried out. (Payment System ECB)

Market Research Analysis.documentation:
Market Research Analysis is the process of systematically gathering, analyzing, and interpreting information about a specific market, including its customers, competitors, and the overall industry. The goal is to gain insights that help businesses make informed decisions regarding their products, services, marketing strategies, and overall business operations.
Purpose:
Specific Insights: Market research analysis is more focused and specific. It involves gathering and analyzing data about a particular target market, customer segment, or product/service to gain insights into consumer behavior, preferences, and needs.
Tactical Insights: It helps businesses understand their customers, refine products or services, and tailor marketing strategies. This analysis is more about tactical decisions rather than broad strategic direction.
Key Components:
Primary Research: Collecting original data through surveys, interviews, focus groups, or observations.
Secondary Research: Analyzing existing data from reports, studies, and other resources.
Customer Insights: Understanding customer needs, preferences, and pain points.
Product/Service Testing: Evaluating customer responses to a product or service.
Competitive Analysis: Assessing customer perceptions of competitors' products/services.
When to Use:
For launching a new product or service.
To refine existing products/services based on customer feedback.
To tailor marketing campaigns and messaging.
For understanding customer satisfaction and loyalty.
Summary
- Market Analysis is broader and focuses on the overall market environment, useful for strategic decisions.
- Market Research Analysis is more detailed and customer-centric, aimed at understanding specific aspects of the market for tactical decisions.

A repurchase agreement, or 'repo', is a short-term agreement to sell securities in order to buy them back at a slightly higher price. (Investopedia)
A repurchase agreement (repo) is a form of short-term borrowing for dealers in government securities. In the case of a repo, a dealer sells government securities to investors, usually on an overnight basis, and buys them back the following day at a slightly higher price. (Investopedia)
Sale of securities together with an agreement for the seller to buy back the securities at a later date.
A repo is equivalent to a spot sale combined with a forward contract. For the seller of the security it is a repo; for the buyer of the security it is a reverse repurchase agreement. (ISO20022)
Agreement between two parties to sell a financial instrument or set of financial instruments and repurchase such instruments at an agreed future date. (ISO20022)
A repurchase agreement (repo) is a short-term secured loan: one party sells securities to another and agrees to repurchase those securities later at a higher price.

Special Pricing Term and Condition.documentation:
A Special Pricing Condition is a bank-authorized override of standard product pricing terms that is applied in response to a strategic campaign, regulatory requirement, or major business event. Unlike product-level discount pricing, where profitability is absorbed within the product, a Special Pricing Condition is usually funded through a campaign or compliance budget so that the shortfall does not distort product-level performance.
Special Pricing Conditions may:
- Temporarily waive or adjust product fees, charges, or interest rates.
- Apply eligibility rules based on campaigns, customer segments, or regulatory directives.
- Include non-product concessions (e.g., vouchers, gifts, service credits).
- Be centrally captured, broadcast, and verified to ensure controlled application across systems.
A Special Pricing Condition is a time-bound, strategic override of standard product pricing, governed at the bank level, and often linked to campaigns or compliance measures  with costs allocated outside the product P&L.

eCommerce Gateway.documentation: An ecommerce payment gateway is a service that authorizes credit card payments and processes them securely with a user's merchant account.

documentation_sections.documentation: An ecommerce payment gateway is a service that authorizes credit card payments and processes them securely with a user's merchant account.

eTrading Workbench Session.documentation: The operation of an eTrading Workbench for a bounded period of time.

documentation_sections.documentation: The operation of an eTrading Workbench for a bounded period of time.

Business Support.documentation: This Business Area spans a wide range of general business management and support activities that may be found in any commercial business and that are therefore not specific to Banking. This area of the Landscape is included for completeness as many banking specific business activities may need to make reference to these more general capabilities.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Area spans a wide range of general business management and support activities that may be found in any commercial business and that are therefore not specific to Banking. This area of the Landscape is included for completeness as many banking specific business activities may need to make reference to these more general capabilities.

Operations and Execution.documentation: This business area includes the full range of product fulfillment activities for wholesale and retail banking, including shared operational capabilities and all front, middle and back office activities.  This is probably excessive in scope and so needs to be divided into several new areas.  There are currently 4 'sub areas' as working places to group the current range of domains in - Retail Products, Wholesale Products Front/Middle Office, Wholesale Products Back Office, Central Operations.

documentation_sections.documentation: This business area includes the full range of product fulfillment activities for wholesale and retail banking, including shared operational capabilities and all front, middle and back office activities.  This is probably excessive in scope and so needs to be divided into several new areas.  There are currently 4 'sub areas' as working places to group the current range of domains in - Retail Products, Wholesale Products Front/Middle Office, Wholesale Products Back Office, Central Operations.

Reference Data.documentation: The Business Area Reference Data contains all categories of managed business reference information, covering subjects including customer details, business partner details and product details. In the case of products it includes aspects of product design, development and quality assurance. It also covers market data feeds for general research and analysis and the range of more specialized trading support market information feeds. This reference information is widely accessed across other activities of the landscape.

Risk and Compliance.documentation: This Business Area covers the analysis and management of business risk, covering group treasury, asset and liability policies, product and market activities. It includes the handling of regulatory compliance and reporting obligations.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Area covers the analysis and management of business risk, covering group treasury, asset and liability policies, product and market activities. It includes the handling of regulatory compliance and reporting obligations.

Sales and Service.documentation: This business area covers all marketing, business development, customer management and sales and servicing activities. It excludes the fulfillment activities associated with in-force product delivery but includes all customer agreement related activities.

documentation_sections.documentation: This business area covers all marketing, business development, customer management and sales and servicing activities. It excludes the fulfillment activities associated with in-force product delivery but includes all customer agreement related activities.

Account Management.documentation: This Business Domain groups together a range of Service Domains that support account and account related services for cash/currency and reward point accounts. It includes account reconciliation, accounts receivable processing and some broader consolidated position management and fraud detection facilities.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain groups together a range of Service Domains that support account and account related services for cash/currency and reward point accounts. It includes account reconciliation, accounts receivable processing and some broader consolidated position management and fraud detection facilities.

Bank Portfolio and Treasury.documentation: This domain draws together the Group Treasury and overall bank portfolio management activities as might be overseen by the bank's asset and liability committee (ALCO) or equivalent policy function. It includes some functions typically related to managing the balance sheet (repos and securitization).

documentation_sections.documentation: This domain draws together the Group Treasury and overall bank portfolio management activities as might be overseen by the bank's asset and liability committee (ALCO) or equivalent policy function. It includes some functions typically related to managing the balance sheet (repos and securitization).

Buildings Equipment and Facilities.documentation: This Business Domain covers all activities associated with the acquisition, administration, operation and maintenance of buildings and non-IT equipment (this can include fleet/transport facilities when appropriate).

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain covers all activities associated with the acquisition, administration, operation and maintenance of buildings and non-IT equipment (this can include fleet/transport facilities when appropriate).

Business Analysis.documentation: This Business Domain consolidates the range of enterprise and divisional performance analysis activities covering general areas such as customer segment and product profitability and more targeted/specialized considerations such as channel. branch portfolio and contribution analysis.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain consolidates the range of enterprise and divisional performance analysis activities covering general areas such as customer segment and product profitability and more targeted/specialized considerations such as channel. branch portfolio and contribution analysis.

Business Command and Control.documentation: This Business Domain contains the range of capabilities associated with the organizational command and control structure of the enterprise. Typically these Service Domains may be repeated and/or may be structured to handle multiple Lines of Business, Legal Entities and/or Business Units (profit/cost centers) as necessary to reflect the specific structure of the enterprise. The command and control structure is derived following the Model Bank approach outlined in the BIAN How To Guides.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain contains the range of capabilities associated with the organizational command and control structure of the enterprise. Typically these Service Domains may be repeated and/or may be structured to handle multiple Lines of Business, Legal Entities and/or Business Units (profit/cost centers) as necessary to reflect the specific structure of the enterprise. The command and control structure is derived following the Model Bank approach outlined in the BIAN How To Guides.

Business Direction.documentation: This Business Domain contains the enterprise's executive functions (policies, strategy and direction) and some enterprise wide tasks such as business architecture and continuity planning.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain contains the enterprise's executive functions (policies, strategy and direction) and some enterprise wide tasks such as business architecture and continuity planning.

Cards.documentation: The Cards Business Domain  contains the fulfillment Service Domains for all cards related products (Credit & Charge). Note that debit cards associated with a current account may leverage some of these capabilities and that many merchant related activities are not fully represented in the model at this stage.

documentation_sections.documentation: The Cards Business Domain  contains the fulfillment Service Domains for all cards related products (Credit & Charge). Note that debit cards associated with a current account may leverage some of these capabilities and that many merchant related activities are not fully represented in the model at this stage.

Channel Specific.documentation: This business domain includes a mixture of service domains that provide the management, configuration and operation of the different channels used by customers to access the products and services of the bank. It includes activities associated with the physical branch network and the movements of physical cash and non-cash inventory.

documentation_sections.documentation: This business domain includes a mixture of service domains that provide the management, configuration and operation of the different channels used by customers to access the products and services of the bank. It includes activities associated with the physical branch network and the movements of physical cash and non-cash inventory.

Collateral Administration.documentation: This Business Domain provides the fairly narrow grouping of Service Domains that support the management allocation and recovery of collateral against a customer.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain provides the fairly narrow grouping of Service Domains that support the management allocation and recovery of collateral against a customer.

Consumer Services.documentation: This Business Domain brings together a number of services typically provided to consumer customers such as remittances, currency exchange, tax, investment and 3rd party product offerings (e.g. insurance). It also handles any consumer tax reporting obligations.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain brings together a number of services typically provided to consumer customers such as remittances, currency exchange, tax, investment and 3rd party product offerings (e.g. insurance). It also handles any consumer tax reporting obligations.

Corporate Financing and Advisory Service.documentation: This Business Domain covers the corporate finance and advisory services offered to corporate clients including corporate finance advice, IPOs, M&A and private and public offerings.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain covers the corporate finance and advisory services offered to corporate clients including corporate finance advice, IPOs, M&A and private and public offerings.

Corporate Relations.documentation: This Business Domain contains Service Domains that handle general corporate communications (with interested parties including investors) and the relationships with key legal and regulatory authorities.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain contains Service Domains that handle general corporate communications (with interested parties including investors) and the relationships with key legal and regulatory authorities.

Cross Channel.documentation: This business domain contains the collection of Service Domains that handle the customer interaction across all possible channels, including customer identity authentication and activity authorization. It supports multiple session/device contacts and enables the leverage of the customer interaction and the build-up and analysis of access history.

documentation_sections.documentation: This business domain contains the collection of Service Domains that handle the customer interaction across all possible channels, including customer identity authentication and activity authorization. It supports multiple session/device contacts and enables the leverage of the customer interaction and the build-up and analysis of access history.

Cross Product Operations.documentation: This Business Domain is a sub category of Operations & Execution that brings together capabilities that tend to be shared across multiple products, often as a centralized operational capability.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain is a sub category of Operations & Execution that brings together capabilities that tend to be shared across multiple products, often as a centralized operational capability.

Document Management and Archive.documentation: This Business Domain provides central document management capabilities - covering bulk mailing (in and out bound) general document scanning, indexing and retrieval services and any physical and electronic distribution and archiving capabilities. It assumes some level of centralization of document handling and digitization for streamlining of production operations.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain provides central document management capabilities - covering bulk mailing (in and out bound) general document scanning, indexing and retrieval services and any physical and electronic distribution and archiving capabilities. It assumes some level of centralization of document handling and digitization for streamlining of production operations.

External Agency.documentation: This Business Domain brings together Service Domains that cover the relationship and agreement details for the range of external business relationships.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain brings together Service Domains that cover the relationship and agreement details for the range of external business relationships.

Finance.documentation: This Business Domain covers the central financial control and reporting activities of the enterprise including division/unit budget negotiations, reporting and financial audit and the assembly and reporting of the financial statements. It also includes enterprise/legal entity tax handling.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain covers the central financial control and reporting activities of the enterprise including division/unit budget negotiations, reporting and financial audit and the assembly and reporting of the financial statements. It also includes enterprise/legal entity tax handling.

Human Resource Management.documentation: This Business Domain brings together the wide range of human resource management functions including recruitment, training, assessment and allocation tasks and the range of employee support functions including payroll & benefits, travel and expenses and employee access controls and authorities.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain brings together the wide range of human resource management functions including recruitment, training, assessment and allocation tasks and the range of employee support functions including payroll & benefits, travel and expenses and employee access controls and authorities.

IT Management.documentation: This Business Domain includes the wide range of IT system operation, development and deployment activities for all production platforms, applications and communications technologies. This includes end user technology and help desk first and second level activities. It also includes the selection and definition of technology plans, policies, guidelines and standards and overall IT financial management and administration.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain includes the wide range of IT system operation, development and deployment activities for all production platforms, applications and communications technologies. This includes end user technology and help desk first and second level activities. It also includes the selection and definition of technology plans, policies, guidelines and standards and overall IT financial management and administration.

Investment Management.documentation: This Business Domain handles investment activity, covering the managed investment portfolios with associated policies and valuation services and self executed eTrading.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain handles investment activity, covering the managed investment portfolios with associated policies and valuation services and self executed eTrading.

Knowledge and Intellectual Property Mana.documentation: This Business Domain supports the banks management and leverage of its intellectual property (IP) assets. This includes the registration/capture of IP, the administration and licensing of IP and infringement detection and responses when necessary.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain supports the banks management and leverage of its intellectual property (IP) assets. This includes the registration/capture of IP, the administration and licensing of IP and infringement detection and responses when necessary.

Loans and Deposits.documentation: This Business Domain contains the Service Domains associated with the fulfillment of the main Loan and Deposit products, it includes the core Current Account or DDA product.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain contains the Service Domains associated with the fulfillment of the main Loan and Deposit products, it includes the core Current Account or DDA product.

Market Data.documentation: This Business Domain covers access to and the internal distribution of the different market research, analysis, news, quote and pricing feeds. This includes the specialized feeds that support trading activity, more general market research and analysis and access to any global directories and information standards.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain covers access to and the internal distribution of the different market research, analysis, news, quote and pricing feeds. This includes the specialized feeds that support trading activity, more general market research and analysis and access to any global directories and information standards.

Market Operations.documentation: This Business Domain combines various back office and support functions for wholesale trading including clearing and settlement and custodial services. It includes trade reporting, valuations and fund administration activities.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain combines various back office and support functions for wholesale trading including clearing and settlement and custodial services. It includes trade reporting, valuations and fund administration activities.

Marketing.documentation: This Business Domain covers new business development activities including prospect and internal campaign design and development, customer surveys and advertising.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain covers new business development activities including prospect and internal campaign design and development, customer surveys and advertising.

Models.documentation: This Business Domain covers the development, certification (where necessary) and deployment of a wide range of models and algorithms that may be used across the bank. It includes market risk and valuation models, business and operational risk, employee and customer behavior analyses, credit decisioning and fraud scanners and detection.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain covers the development, certification (where necessary) and deployment of a wide range of models and algorithms that may be used across the bank. Non-IT and Non-HR Enterprise Services.documentation: This Business Domain brings together a collection of general non-IT related support services including internal audit, security and legal advisory services, supplier management and procurement, fixed asset register and company billing and payments.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain brings together a collection of general non-IT related support services including internal audit, security and legal advisory services, supplier management and procurement, fixed asset register and company billing and payments.

Operational Services.documentation: This Business Domain brings together a number of general back office services that provide cross product support not directly matched to the other Business Domains in this Business Area.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain brings together a number of general back office services that provide cross product support not directly matched to the other Business Domains in this Business Area.

Party.documentation: This Business Domain covers the different party/customer reference information that is maintained by the bank for its institutional, corporate and consumer customers.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain covers the different party/customer reference information that is maintained by the bank for its institutional, corporate and consumer customers.

Payments.documentation: This Business Domain groups the Service Domains supporting payment transactions, including the various connections to payment networks, central cash management and check processing.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain groups the Service Domains supporting payment transactions, including the various connections to payment networks, central cash management and check processing.

Product Specific Fulfillment.documentation: This Business Domain is a sub category of the Operations & Execution Business Area that includes all fulfillment and operational tasks associated with the bank's products and services. Product Specific Fulfillment covers the product specific activities associated with the main groups of banking products.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain is a sub category of the Operations & Execution Business Area that includes all fulfillment and operational tasks associated with the bank's products and services. Product Specific Fulfillment covers the product specific activities associated with the main groups of banking products.

Regulations and Compliance.documentation: This Business Domain covers the interpretation support, compliance assurance and regulatory reporting obligations of the bank, including ad-hoc compliance resolution when necessary. Note that general relations with the regulatory authorities are handled at an enterprise level elsewhere in the landscape.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain covers the interpretation support, compliance assurance and regulatory reporting obligations of the bank, including ad-hoc compliance resolution when necessary. Note that general relations with the regulatory authorities are handled at an enterprise level elsewhere in the landscape.

Sales.documentation: This Business Domain covers all aspects of sales planning, campaign execution prospect and opportunity management, product matching and offer processing, including product specialist sales support and commission handling.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain covers all aspects of sales planning, campaign execution prospect and opportunity management, product matching and offer processing, including product specialist sales support and commission handling.

Servicing.documentation: This Business Domain brings together the fulfillment capabilities for various customer servicing support functions in particular customer case resolution and analysis and customer orders (customer related actions that span product and services).

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain brings together the fulfillment capabilities for various customer servicing support functions in particular customer case resolution and analysis and customer orders (customer related actions that span product and services).

Trade Banking.documentation: This Business Domain brings together a broad range of trade banking product and service fulfillment Service Domains covering trade finance and the many different cash management services that might be offered.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain brings together a broad range of trade banking product and service fulfillment Service Domains covering trade finance and the many different cash management services that might be offered.

Wholesale Trading.documentation: This Business Domain covers a broad range of front office and middle office wholesale trading activities across all major instrument categories (FX/money market, equities, securities, commodities, derivatives). It also covers basic primary market functions such as equity/debt issuance and trading.

documentation_sections.documentation: This Business Domain covers a broad range of front office and middle office wholesale trading activities across all major instrument categories (FX/money market, equities, securities, commodities, derivatives). It also covers basic primary market functions such as equity/debt issuance and trading.

Customer Management.documentation: Ability to define, control, predict, process, organize, present, and analyze all aspects of information, documents, preferences, experiences, and history related to an individual or other legal entity that has, plans to have, has had, or is a recipient or beneficiary of a legally binding agreement with the organization.

Product Management.documentation: Ability to conceptualize, design, develop, bundle, source, maintain, and retire a named combination of goods and services that can be offered to customers, in whole or in part, to satisfy the customer's overall needs and desires.

documentation_sections.documentation: Ability to conceptualize, design, develop, bundle, source, maintain, and retire a named combination of goods and services that can be offered to customers, in whole or in part, to satisfy the customer's overall needs and desires.
